title: Symmetric Tree
description:
Given the `root` of a binary tree, check whether it is a **mirror of itself** (i.e., symmetric around its center).

Return `true` if the left subtree is a structural and value-wise mirror image of the right subtree, and `false` otherwise.
hints: Checking whether a tree is symmetric reduces to checking whether `root.left` and `root.right` are mirror images of each other.
Two trees `a` and `b` are mirrors if both are `null`, or if neither is `null`, `a.val == b.val`, `a.left` mirrors `b.right`, and `a.right` mirrors `b.left`.
Be careful: a palindromic inorder traversal does NOT guarantee symmetry because structure matters.

examples.explanation: Left subtree [2, 3, 4] and right subtree [2, 4, 3] are exact mirror images.
Both 2s have only a right child (3), so the tree is not symmetric around the center.
A single-node tree is trivially symmetric.
